mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 2.5% over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 2.5% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 6% for two consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative during periods when UNRATE < 6% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent contraction in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in industrial production (INDPRO) and a fall in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 2% over three months signals a shift from consumer-durable manufacturing to residential construction weakness, which historically precedes a relative underperformance of cyclical equities and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO rises >2% and HOUST falls <-2% over three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 1% combined with a concurrent rise in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 3% signals a monetary policy lag and inflation surprise, which erodes real purchasing power and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% AND CPIAUCSL > 3% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when FEDFUNDS < 1% and CPIAUCSL > 3% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 200,000 per month for five consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive during periods of five consecutive months with PAYEMS > 200,000.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 1% over two consecutive months signals a broad-based demand shock, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 < -1% and RSAFS < -1% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when both GDPC1 and RSAFS fall by more than 1% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above 3% for three consecutive months signals an acceleration in supply capacity, which historically coincides with improved earnings expectations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, except during periods of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 4%).
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 3% for 3 consecutive months AND CPIAUCSL <= 4%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive when INDPRO > 3% for three months and CPIAUCSL <= 4%, or if returns are positive but CPIAUCSL > 4% in the same period.
